h: Plan your splash and explore the city
p: A bit of planning makes for a better day. Pack swimwear, towels, flip-flops for walking around and a change of warm clothes for afterwards. Goggles are useful for younger swimmers, and a waterproof phone pouch is handy for photos. Lockers keep valuables safe, and it's worth grabbing one early so you're not hanging around once you're changed.

Book your session in advance, especially at weekends and in the school holidays, when the most popular times sell out. Check height and age rules for the bigger rides together before you go, so nobody's disappointed at the top of the stairs.
How long to allow? Your session sets the pace, but arrive early to get changed without rushing. Younger children will need breaks, so plan in time to warm up and grab a snack.

The LC sits in Swansea's Maritime Quarter, right next to the National Waterfront Museum, which tells the story of Wales's industrial and maritime history with plenty of hands-on displays for families. Swansea Museum, a grand Victorian building full of curiosities, is close by too, along with the Dylan Thomas Centre for anyone curious about the city's most famous poet.

In the city centre, Swansea Market is a must for food lovers, with fresh Welsh cakes, laverbread and cockles among the local specialities. If the weather's good, head west along the bay to Mumbles, where the pier, ice cream parlours and little shops make for a lovely stroll.

Further afield, the Gower Peninsula offers some of the most beautiful beaches in Britain, including Rhossili Bay with its sweeping sands and views of Worms Head. It's well worth a day of its own if you're staying a little longer.
